details.exam_pattern: High. CT561 is predictable at both topic and question-type level. The scenario changes, but the required moves stay very similar: draw a stock-flow model, identify feedback, do simple integration, explain a system-dynamics structure, or extend an SIR/public-health model.
details.title: CT561 - Systems Modelling and Simulation
exam_block: Most reviewed papers ask 3 questions out of 4.
2024/25 and 2025/26 keep the same broad structure.
The paper consistently rewards knowing reusable model patterns rather than memorising one-off facts.
Past papers are useful because the starred lecturer has stayed stable across the whole reviewed archive.
drill: Stock-and-flow modelling is the core repeat area: stocks, inflows, outflows, auxiliaries, equations and translating text scenarios into models.
Feedback loops recur heavily: link polarity, loop polarity, balancing/reinforcing loops, workload pressure, correction loops and side effects.
Graphical/Euler integration is high-value: net-flow calculation, stock graphs, DT choice, integration error and why smaller DT improves approximation.
SIR/public-health modelling is one of the safest targets: infection/recovery flows, force of infection, R0, herd immunity and extensions such as vaccination or quarantine.
Stock management and workforce models recur: anchor/adjustment structures, recruitment, workforce pipelines, aging chains, target stock and adjustment time.
Supporting marks often come from Vensim terminology, validation, policy sensitivity, equilibrium, Little's Law, delays and smoothing.

families.title: Graphical Integration, Euler Method and Error
appearances: 2022/23 Q4(a) [12]: constant outflow 50, initial stock 150; draw stock-flow and net flow, then graphically integrate from 0 to 20, explaining behaviour when inflow equals outflow at 2.5, 10 and 17.5.

2022/23 Q4(c) [5]: describe Euler assumptions and calculate integration error for dS/dt=4t over 5 time units with DT=1.

2023/24 Q4(a) [12]: constant outflow 50; regular inflow 100 to 0 over five time units. Draw stock-flow including net flow, calculate net flow, and graphically integrate the stock with behaviour modes.
2023/24 Q4(b) [5]: describe Euler and assumptions; for linear net flow, state when it overestimates.
2023/24 Q4(c) [8]: calculate stock using Euler with DT=5 .
2024/25 Q4(a) [12]: two constant inflows, 30 and 20 units/minute, against a sawtooth outflow. Draw, calculate net flow, graphical integration and behaviour modes.
2024/25 Q4(b) [5]: state when Euler underestimates and support it over 0-5.
2024/25 Q4(c) [8]: Euler with DT=10 .
2025/26 Q1(a) [12]: variable inflow and constant 50 units/day outflow; stock starts at 100 and may go negative.
2025/26 Q1(b) [5]: state when Euler overestimates and support it over 0-2.5 with DT=0.5 .
2025/26 Q1(c) [8]: Euler with DT=5 .
families.question: Given inflow/outflow graph(s), draw the stock-flow model including net flow; calculate net flow; integrate it graphically to plot the stock and explain each behaviour mode. Then describe forward Euler, its assumptions and error direction, and calculate the Euler stock at the stated DT.
families.answer: Complete answer must contain: Net Flow = Inflow - Outflow ; Stock = INTEG(Net Flow, Initial Stock) ; a stock rectangle, material flow pipes and an auxiliary net-flow variable. For linear sections use trapezoid area ((NF_start + NF_end)/2) x elapsed time . Plot stock at endpoints, zero crossings and slope changes. State: stock rises/falls by the sign of net flow, reaches a turning point where net flow is zero, and changes curvature where net flow changes direction. Euler method: S(t+DT)=S(t)+NF(t) x DT . It treats net flow as constant over DT, therefore stock change as linear, and needs DT small enough for the approximation. Forward Euler uses the left endpoint: it overestimates a falling linear net flow and underestimates a rising linear net flow. Show the supplied support calculation as a sum of start-of-step rectangles, then compare it with the exact triangular/trapezoidal area.

families.title: Workload Backlog Model, Feedback Polarity and Policy Analysis
appearances: 2023/24 Q1(a) [8]: infer reinforcing versus balancing one-stock structures from an accelerating-growth graph and a goal-seeking curve.
2023/24 Q1(b,c) [10,7]: order-fulfilment backlog, work pressure, time per task, workweek and fatigue; show polarities and identify the workweek side-effect loop.
2024/25 Q1(a) [5]: define feedback and its two types; explain why feedback structures improve stock-flow models.
2024/25 Q1(b,c) [12,8]: Assignment Backlog with Allocated, Rework and Completed; name three negative policy loops and two positive side-effect loops, tracing each from increasing backlog.
2025/26 Q3(a) [6]: define link polarity, loop polarity and feedback from the environmental-quality example, then discuss generated behaviour.
2025/26 Q3(b,c) [12,7]: Claims Backlog with New Claims, Reworked Claims and Claims Completed; identify three policy loops and three side-effect loops and recommend a response.
families.question: Construct a signed stock-flow model of a backlog under work pressure. Identify intended balancing policies and reinforcing side-effects; prove each loop polarity by tracing an increase through the full closed loop; then discuss the best policy response.
families.answer: Construction: first write the stock equation, for example Backlog = INTEG(New Work + Rework - Completed, Initial Backlog) . Use pipes for named inflows/outflows. Add Work Pressure, Time per Task/Claim, Workweek, Temporary Staff, Fatigue and quality/rework only as auxiliaries and signed information links. Polarity proof: a positive link means variables move in the same direction; a negative link means opposite directions, all else equal. A loop with an odd number of negative links is balancing; an even number is reinforcing. Still write the verbal increase-trace: a rising backlog raises pressure, a policy raises completion, and completion lowers backlog, so the final effect opposes the initial rise. Policy answer: distinguish immediate balancing capacity responses from delayed reinforcing side-effects. Shorter time per task can raise rework; longer workweek can raise fatigue and reduce completion; untrained temporary staff can reduce productivity. Recommend a policy only after naming its mechanism, delay, intended outcome and quality/capacity trade-off.

families.title: SIR/Public-Health Calculations, Proofs and Extensions

2022/23 Q3(b) [12]: extend SIR to mild, moderate and severe infected stocks with 50% mild infectiousness, antiviral transfers, first-order hospital delays, equations, units and feedbacks.
2022/23 Q3(c) [5]: explain how the antiviral transfer equation changes hospital admissions between scenarios.
2023/24 Q3(a) [10]: explain infection and recovery equations and derive the equilibrium condition c i d = 1 , assuming S=N .
2023/24 Q3(b) [15]: build a seven-stock SEI2H2R model with asymptomatic/symptomatic infection, hospital delay, different infectiousness and equations.
2024/25 Q3(a) [5]: calculate force of infection and herd-immunity threshold from N=10,000 , 2% infectious, R0=12 , D=7 .
2024/25 Q3(b) [15]: SIR plus quarantine fraction, control flag, equations, feedbacks and explanation of force of infection.
2024/25 Q3(c) [5]: modify the model for young and elderly cohorts.
2025/26 Q2(b) [12]: SIR countermeasures: 20% of infection flow to quarantine, vaccinated stock, goal-seeking vaccination fraction, attack rate, equations and feedbacks.
2025/26 Q2(c) [5]: bubble plot of final attack rate by quarantine fraction and final vaccination fraction.
families.question: Build or extend a compartmental infection model with equations and feedbacks, calculate/derive the requested reproduction or threshold measure, and explain exactly how an intervention changes transmission, recovery or susceptibility.
families.answer: Core construction: lambda = beta I/N , Infections = lambda S = beta I S/N , Recoveries = I/D ; then S=INTEG(-Infections,S0) , I=INTEG(Infections-Recoveries,I0) , R=INTEG(Recoveries,R0) . If paper notation is c , i , d , use beta=c i and R0=c i d . Explain units: lambda is per susceptible per time; infection/recovery flows are people per time. Required proof pattern: at the infection peak, set dI/dt=0 , so beta I S/N=I/D . For I>0 , divide by I and use R0=beta D , giving S/N=1/R0 . In a wholly susceptible equilibrium, set S=N to obtain c i d=1 ; an outbreak grows when the corresponding reproduction number exceeds 1. Extension distinction: 2024/25 moves a stated fraction of Infectious people to quarantine and uses a 0/1 control flag. 2025/26 explicitly splits the infection flow : To Q=QF lambda S , To I=(1-QF) lambda S , and quarantined people do not infect. Do not silently replace one construction with the other. Vaccination is a flow from S to Vaccinated; if its fraction is goal-seeking, give its adjustment equation. For cohorts, replicate S/I/R by group and specify within/between-group infection terms or a contact matrix.

families.title: Stock Management, Staff Recruitment and Ageing Chains
appearances: 2022/23 Q2(b) [7]: show why employee target is unreachable with resignations under adjustment alone; add an information delay as the replacement-flow anchor.
2022/23 Q2(c) [10]: model Rookie and Experienced staff with hires, quits, promotions, progression delays and quit fractions.
2023/24 Q2(b) [5]: describe anchor and adjustment and identify the general structure used for each.
2023/24 Q2(c) [12]: consulting startup with Rookie and Experienced stocks, 12-month progression delay, attrition and target-driven recruitment.
2024/25 Q2(b) [7]: extend adjustment-to-goal to stock management, describe anchor/adjustment and show anchor delay.
2024/25 Q2(c) [12]: University staff recruitment: Staff starts at 500, Students 10,000, desired ratio falls 20 to 10 at time 10; predict staff and identify settling-speed auxiliary.
2025/26 Q4(a) [5]: add expected University enrolments to a supplied stock-flow model with equations.
2025/26 Q4(b) [5]: compare adjustment-to-goal and stock management, stating their key difference, anchor and adjustment.
2025/26 Q4(c,d) [10,5]: Trainee, Experienced and Senior pharmaceutical workforce, stage attrition/progression, then target drops 300 to 100 and equations/behaviour must be sketched.
families.question: Explain stock management as expected replacement plus correction of the desired-actual gap, then construct a workforce model with equations, feedbacks, delays and the response to a changed target.
families.answer: Core equations: Discrepancy=Desired Stock-Actual Stock ; Adjustment=Discrepancy/Adjustment Time ; Expected Losses=SMOOTH(Actual Losses, Expectation Adjustment Time) ; Required Inflow=Expected Losses+Adjustment . The anchor replaces expected normal losses, whereas adjustment closes a current target gap. At equilibrium, adjustment is zero and required inflow equals expected loss. University construction: Desired Staff=Students/Desired Student-Staff Ratio ; Staff=INTEG(Hires-Quits,500) ; Quits=Quit Fraction x Staff ; Hires=Expected Quits+(Desired Staff-Staff)/Staff Adjustment Time . At 10,000 students and ratio 20, desired staff is 500. A ratio of 10 changes target to 1,000, so Staff rises towards 1,000 at a decreasing rate. The staff adjustment time most directly sets response speed. Ageing-chain construction: add progression flows Trainees/12 and Experienced/36 (or the paper's stated delays), one attrition flow per stage, and Total Staff as the sum. A lower target makes adjustment negative; if no dismissal flow exists, bound hires at zero and explain that attrition/progression determine the reduction speed.

families.title: Fractional Rates, Adjustment to a Goal and Smoothing
appearances: 2022/23 Q2(a) [8]: estimate a fractional increase rate from a stock graph starting at 1,000 and state assumptions.
2023/24 Q2(a) [8]: build a stock-flow structure that produces a smoothed version of a random input and explain adjustment time.
2024/25 Q2(a) [6]: describe with examples fractional increase rate, fractional decrease rate and adjustment to a goal.
2025/26 Q2(a) [8]: modify a fractional decrease flow where decrease fraction G is itself an adjustment-to-goal structure approaching maximum G* ; comment on a real context.
families.question: State the flow formula, units and expected behaviour for fractional growth/decline or adjustment; when a rate itself changes, make that rate a goal-seeking state rather than treating it as an instant constant.
families.answer: Formulas: Increase=Stock x Fractional Increase Rate , Decrease=Stock x Fractional Decrease Rate , Adjustment=(Goal-Actual)/Adjustment Time . A fraction has units 1/time , so the resulting flow has stock units/time. Constant fractional rates produce exponential behaviour. Smoothing/variable rate: Smoothed=INTEG((Input-Smoothed)/AT, Initial Smoothed) . For the 2025/26 varying decrease fraction, use G=INTEG((G*-G)/AT,G0) and Outflow=S x G . State that larger AT responds more slowly and smooths more strongly; do not call it a simple moving average.

families.title: Current-Format Variants Worth Keeping Separate
appearances: 2022/23 Q1(a) [5]: list three stock-and-flow principles and illustrate a Carbon in the Atmosphere stock with inflows and outflows.
2022/23 Q1(b) [10]: model customer and staff stocks, the customer-to-staff ratio, attractiveness, recruitment, hiring, morale and staff leaving, without equations.
2022/23 Q1(c) [10]: trace and calculate feedback-loop polarity; identify the loop supporting sustained company growth.

2023/24 Q1(a) [8]: infer one-stock feedback structure from behaviour graph. Accelerating growth suggests reinforcing fractional growth; approach to a limit suggests balancing adjustment/capacity feedback.

2025/26 Q4(a) [5]: extend a supplied University model with expected enrolments. Add a stock only if enrolments are delayed/forecast; otherwise formulate the stated expected-enrolment auxiliary and its link to the relevant flow.

2025/26 Q2(c) [5]: plot quarantine fraction against final vaccination fraction using circle size for final attack rate. Put largest circles at low quarantine/low vaccination and smallest at high/high, then explain the monotone policy mechanism and any interaction.

cards.back: NF = Inflow - Outflow ; Stock = INTEG(NF, Initial Stock) . NF: stock/time; Stock: stock.
Delta Stock = ((NF_start + NF_end)/2) x Delta t on a linear interval. Add signed area to the previous stock.

cards.front: Read a stock from net flow?
cards.back: NF > 0 : rising; NF < 0 : falling. A + to - crossing is a stock maximum; a - to + crossing is a minimum.
Accelerating growth: reinforcing, e.g. Inflow = k x Stock . Approach to a limit: balancing, e.g. goal seeking/carrying capacity.
S(t+DT) = S(t) + NF(t) x DT . Use start-of-step NF; treat it as constant over a sufficiently small DT.

cards.front: Euler error direction for linear NF?
cards.back: Falling NF: forward Euler overestimates. Rising NF: forward Euler underestimates.
For each DT: write t , NF(t) , NF x DT , then next S = current S + change .
+ link: cause and effect move together; - link: opposite. Odd negative links = balancing; even = reinforcing.
Reinforcing amplifies change. Balancing opposes change or closes a gap. Confirm with an increase-trace.
It explains behaviour, delays, side-effects and policy resistance; rates are not independent inputs.
Backlog = INTEG(New Work + Rework - Completed, Initial Backlog) . Pressure, fatigue and workweek are auxiliaries.
Backlog + -> Pressure + -> Capacity/effort + -> Completed + -> Backlog - : one negative link, so balancing.

Rework: less Time per Task -> more Rework. Fatigue: more Workweek -> more Fatigue -> less Completed. Claims model: more Temporary Staff -> more Time per Claim -> less Completed. Each closes a reinforcing backlog loop.
Name the balancing benefit, delayed reinforcing side-effects and affected outcome; test backlog, completion, rework, fatigue and capacity together.
Flow = Stock x Fractional Rate ; rate units are 1/time . Constant positive increase gives exponential growth; constant decrease gives exponential decay.
Adjustment = (Goal - Actual)/AT ; Smoothed = INTEG((Input - Smoothed)/AT, Initial Smoothed) . Larger AT = slower response.
G = INTEG((G* - G)/AT, G0) ; Outflow = Stock x G . The rate, not only the stock, is goal seeking.
Anchor replaces expected loss: Expected Losses = SMOOTH(Actual Losses, EAT) . Adjustment closes gap: (Desired - Actual)/AT . Required Inflow = Expected Losses + Adjustment .

cards.front: Desired University staff and target shock?
cards.back: Desired Staff = Students / Desired Student-Staff Ratio . At 10,000 students, ratio 20 -> 500; ratio 10 -> 1,000. Lower ratio means more staff required.
Staff = INTEG(Hires - Quits, Staff0) ; Quits = Quit Fraction x Staff ; Hires = Expected Quits + (Desired Staff - Staff)/Staff AT .
Trainees -> Experienced -> Seniors ; each stage has attrition. Progress = stock/delay ; Total Staff = T + E + S .

cards.front: What if the staff target falls and there is no dismissal flow?
cards.back: Adjustment becomes negative; constrain hires to zero. Staff then falls through attrition, so delays determine reduction speed.
λ=βI/N ; F inf =λS ; F rec =I/D . S=INTEG(−F inf ,S(0)) ; I=INTEG(F inf −F rec ,I(0)) ; R=INTEG(F rec ,R(0)) .
β=ci ; R 0 =βd=cid . With S=N , an outbreak grows when R 0 >1 .
λ=βI/N , units 1/time ; F inf =λS , people/time. p c =1−1/R 0 .
I → F inf → I : reinforcing. F inf → S↓ → F inf ↓ and I → F rec → I↓ : balancing.
2024/25: I → Q , controlled by u∈{0,1} . 2025/26: F Q =qλS , F I =(1−q)λS ; Q does not transmit.

cards.front: Vaccination, attack rate and policy plot?
cards.back: F vax =vS , S → V ; AR=(I+Q+R)/N . Bubble plot: x=q , y=v , size =AR ; largest at low q,v .
Replicate states: (S y ,I y ,R y ) , (S e ,I e ,R e ) ; add within-/between-cohort contact terms or a contact matrix.
S → E → I a /I s ; I a → R , I s → R/H . H : second-order delay; I a infectiousness =0.5I s .
C=M×p ; F vax =min(U,V,C) , where U =unvaccinated and V =available vaccines.
x*=x/x ref ; Rate=Rate ref ×Effect(x*) . Effect is dimensionless.
L=λW : average stock = average throughput × average delay, at equilibrium.
dS/dt=t , S(0)=0 ⇒ S(t)=t²/2 . dP/dt=rP(1−P/C)−sP . Constant g : T 2 =ln(2)/g .

cards.front: In the 2022/23 Q4 graph, what happens to stock at t=2.5, 10 and 17.5?
cards.back: At each time inflow equals the constant outflow of 50, so net flow is zero and the stock's slope is zero. Use the net-flow sign on each side to decide whether each point is a maximum or minimum.

cards.front: For dS/dt = 4t from t=0 to 5, what does forward Euler with DT=1 miss?
cards.back: Its five left-endpoint steps add 4 × (0+1+2+3+4) = 40; exact integration adds 50. It underestimates the stock increase by 10 because the flow rises during every step.

cards.front: Why does hire rate = (target staff − staff)/adjustment time miss a positive target when staff resign?
cards.back: At the target the hire rate falls to zero while resignations continue, so staff fall below target. Add expected resignations as the replacement-flow anchor, with the gap correction as the adjustment.

cards.front: In 2022/23 Q3(a), what is λ when 2% of 100,000 people are infectious, R₀=12 and D=7 days?
cards.back: β = R₀/D = 12/7 per day; λ = βI/N = (12/7) × 0.02 ≈ 0.0343 per day per susceptible. The population count cancels after converting 2% to I/N.

cards.front: How should a model combine mild, moderate and severe infection in force of infection when mild cases are half as infectious?
cards.back: Use effective infectious people = 0.5 × mild + moderate + severe. Then λ = (contacts × infectivity/N) × effective infectious people, before multiplying by susceptibles for the infection flow.

cards.front: How is a latent stage represented when infected people are not yet infectious?
cards.back: Add an Exposed stock between Susceptible and Infectious. New infections enter Exposed; progression after the latent delay enters Infectious, so Exposed does not contribute to transmission until it progresses.

sheets.title: Continuous/System-Dynamics versus Agent-Based Simulation
mistakes: "Many people" does not automatically mean an agent-based model.
More detail does not automatically mean more valid.
Do not present a hybrid model unless you can say which mechanism belongs in each component and how they exchange information.

sheets.title: Vensim, Validation and Policy Analysis
mistakes: A historical fit alone does not validate causal structure.
Reducing DT improves numerical approximation; it does not validate the model.
One simulation run is not a policy recommendation.
Do not discuss policy without naming the flow, parameter or feedback it changes.
